lines.text: A tree stands on the edge of a yard, exactly as far from one corner as from another.
lines.caption: A tree stands on the edge of a yard, exactly as far from one corner as from another.

lines.text: Where is it? A right triangle is hiding in the yard, and it tells us.
lines.caption: Where is it? A right triangle is hiding in the yard, and it tells us.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find that tree.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find that tree.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A rectangular yard A B C D has A B equal to sixteen meters, and B C equal to eight meters.
lines.caption: A rectangular yard A B C D has A B equal to sixteen meters, and B C equal to eight meters.

lines.text: A tree at point E on side A B
lines.caption: A tree at point E on side A B

lines.text: is the same distance from A as from C.
lines.caption: is the same distance from A as from C.

lines.text: How far is the tree from A, in meters?
lines.caption: How far is the tree from A, in meters?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we know? The distance from E to A equals the distance from E to C.
lines.caption: So what do we know? The distance from E to A equals the distance from E to C.

lines.text: E A runs along the bottom. E C is slanted, and it makes a right triangle with the corner B.
lines.caption: E A runs along the bottom. E C is slanted, and it makes a right triangle with the corner B.

lines.text: We want E A.
lines.caption: We want E A.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: test each choice with the Pythagorean theorem.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: test each choice with the Pythagorean theorem.

lines.text: Triangle E B C has a right angle at B. So E B squared plus eight squared equals E C squared.
lines.caption: Triangle E B C has a right angle at B. So E B squared plus eight squared equals E C squared.

lines.text: And E C must equal E A. So E B squared plus sixty-four must equal E A squared.
lines.caption: And E C must equal E A. So E B squared plus sixty-four must equal E A squared.

lines.text: Try six. Then E B is ten, and ten squared plus sixty-four is one hundred sixty-four.
lines.caption: Try six. Then E B is ten, and ten squared plus sixty-four is one hundred sixty-four.

lines.text: But six squared is just thirty-six.
lines.caption: But six squared is just thirty-six.

lines.text: Try eight. Then E B is eight, and eight squared plus sixty-four is one hundred twenty-eight.
lines.caption: Try eight. Then E B is eight, and eight squared plus sixty-four is one hundred twenty-eight.

lines.text: Eight squared is only sixty-four.
lines.caption: Eight squared is only sixty-four.

lines.text: Try ten. Then E B is six. Six squared plus sixty-four is one hundred.
lines.caption: Try ten. Then E B is six. Six squared plus sixty-four is one hundred.

lines.text: And ten squared is one hundred. A match!
lines.caption: And ten squared is one hundred. A match!

lines.text: Triangle E B C has sides six, eight and ten, so E C is ten, just like E A.
lines.caption: Triangle E B C has sides six, eight and ten, so E C is ten, just like E A.

lines.text: The tree is ten meters from A. That's Choice C!
lines.caption: The tree is ten meters from A. That's Choice C!

lines.text: Here's a way that works even without choices. Call the distance x.
lines.caption: Here's a way that works even without choices. Call the distance x.

lines.text: Then E C is also x, and E B is sixteen minus x.
lines.caption: Then E C is also x, and E B is sixteen minus x.

lines.text: The right triangle says sixteen minus x, squared, plus eight squared, equals x squared.
lines.caption: The right triangle says sixteen minus x, squared, plus eight squared, equals x squared.

lines.text: Sixteen minus x, times sixteen minus x, is two hundred fifty-six, minus sixteen x, minus sixteen x, plus x squared.
lines.caption: Sixteen minus x, times sixteen minus x, is two hundred fifty-six, minus sixteen x, minus sixteen x, plus x squared.

lines.text: Sixteen minus x, squared, opens up to two hundred fifty-six, minus thirty-two x, plus x squared.
lines.caption: Sixteen minus x, squared, opens up to two hundred fifty-six, minus thirty-two x, plus x squared.

lines.text: Add sixty-four. Now there's an x squared on both sides, so they cancel out.
lines.caption: Add sixty-four. Now there's an x squared on both sides, so they cancel out.

lines.text: That leaves three hundred twenty equals thirty-two x. So x is ten. Same answer!
lines.caption: That leaves three hundred twenty equals thirty-two x. So x is ten. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When there are no choices to test, or the numbers aren't nice.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When there are no choices to test, or the numbers aren't nice.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice A, six, is a real length: it's E B, from the tree to B. But we want the distance from A.
lines.caption: Choice A, six, is a real length: it's E B, from the tree to B. But we want the distance from A.

lines.text: Choice B, eight, is the short side B C. And we just saw eight fails the test.
lines.caption: Choice B, eight, is the short side B C. And we just saw eight fails the test.

lines.text: Choices D and E, twelve and fourteen: the length E B is only four, then two, and the numbers don't match.
lines.caption: Choices D and E, twelve and fourteen: the length E B is only four, then two, and the numbers don't match.

lines.text: Eighty versus one hundred forty-four, and sixty-eight versus one hundred ninety-six.
lines.caption: Eighty versus one hundred forty-four, and sixty-eight versus one hundred ninety-six.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. When two distances are equal, write one of them a second way, with a right triangle.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. When two distances are equal, write one of them a second way, with a right triangle.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? A bigger yard has A B equal to eighteen meters and B C equal to twelve meters.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? A bigger yard has A B equal to eighteen meters and B C equal to twelve meters.

lines.text: A tree at E on side A B is the same distance from A as from C. How far is it from A?
lines.caption: A tree at E on side A B is the same distance from A as from C. How far is it from A?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's call it x again. E B is eighteen minus x, and B C is twelve.
lines.caption: Let's call it x again. E B is eighteen minus x, and B C is twelve.

lines.text: Eighteen minus x, times eighteen minus x, is three hundred twenty-four, minus eighteen x, twice, plus x squared.
lines.caption: Eighteen minus x, times eighteen minus x, is three hundred twenty-four, minus eighteen x, twice, plus x squared.

lines.text: Eighteen minus x, squared, is three hundred twenty-four, minus thirty-six x, plus x squared.
lines.caption: Eighteen minus x, squared, is three hundred twenty-four, minus thirty-six x, plus x squared.

lines.text: Add one hundred forty-four, and the x squared terms cancel.
lines.caption: Add one hundred forty-four, and the x squared terms cancel.

lines.text: That leaves four hundred sixty-eight equals thirty-six x. So x is thirteen!
lines.caption: That leaves four hundred sixty-eight equals thirty-six x. So x is thirteen!

lines.text: Check: E B is five, and a five, twelve, thirteen triangle is a right triangle. It works!
lines.caption: Check: E B is five, and a five, twelve, thirteen triangle is a right triangle. It works!

lines.text: If you got thirteen meters, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you got thirteen meters, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Name the unknown distance. Then write the same distance a second way, with the Pythagorean theorem.
lines.caption: Name the unknown distance. Then write the same distance a second way, with the Pythagorean theorem.

lines.text: Set the two equal, and solve.
lines.caption: Set the two equal, and solve.
